summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic opiate use, and asthma was admitted for abdominal pain and shortness of breath after resuming alcohol use. He was treated for alcohol withdrawal with Ativan taper, managed for an asthma exacerbation with steroids and antibiotics, and evaluated for abdominal pain, which was attributed to alcoholic gastritis after a CT scan showed no acute pathology. His methadone was continued, and he was stabilized on supportive care. Liver enzymes showed mild elevation with a downtrend. He improved clinically, was discharged home with a short course of pain medication, and advised to follow up for an EGD and substance use counseling.
problems: Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
